task.title: Materialize a persisted recurrence occurrence through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/891 by exposing exact revision-bound recurrence-occurrence task materialization through deterministic writable CLI JSON.
acceptance_criteria: Validate recurrence and task identities before opening writable storage and require the caller's observed occurrence revision.
Delegate atomic materialization to the recurrence store and emit complete recurrence, occurrence revision, and task binding provenance.
Emit one escaped deterministic diagnostic and no stdout for missing, stale, already-materialized, collision, storage, replay, append, or serialization failures.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused success test failed because materialize was not a recognized recurrence subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added integration tests for durable success and reopen, exact output, identity validation, missing and stale evidence, collisions, duplicate materialization, atomicity, and deterministic failure output.

attempts.diagnostic: Creating tasks separately or deriving occurrence state in the CLI would bypass the kernel's revision and atomicity contract.
attempts.patch: Added recurrence materialize, opened the selected store writable only after identity validation, delegated to RecurrenceStore::materialize_occurrence, serialized exact provenance, and documented the boundary in ADR-0051 and scheduler guidance.

attempts.summary: Applied review refactoring and held the exact head through throttling.
attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit identified duplicated occurrence-field mapping; after the fix, the incremental exact-head review was rate limited and its green status was not genuine merge evidence.
attempts.patch: Reused recurrence_occurrence_inspection for shared fields, reran just verify and the Rust quality gate, kept auto-merge disabled through the cooldown, and merged only after CodeRabbit completed a genuine exact-head incremental review with zero unresolved threads.

outcome.summary: Operators can atomically bind one exact persisted recurrence occurrence to a caller-owned task through deterministic CLI JSON without granting scheduling or execution policy.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0177-recurrence-occurrence-materialization-cli.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 177 records: 177 valid, 0 invalid

lessons: Writable CLI commands should validate simple identities before opening storage and leave revision, replay, and atomicity decisions to the kernel.
Successful output should include the caller-observed transition result, including occurrence revision and bound task identity, rather than reconstruct it independently.
Shared occurrence inspection prevents read and write JSON projections from drifting as provenance fields evolve.
Exact-head Rust success does not override a rate-limited automated review; the green status remains false until a genuine incremental review completes.
The command grants one exact provenance binding only, not recurrence selection, clocks, catch-up, due policy, dispatch, retry, or execution authority.
